brief: In 1555 Mary Tudor tried to confirm the return of England to the Catholic fold by executing a number of leading Protestants. In fact this action, more than anything else, undermined Mary’s popularity, gave the Protestant cause a heroic status, and left a lasting legacy of anti-Catholic bigotry in England for many years. The most prominent of these martyrs were Nicholas Ridley, Bishop of London, and Hugh Latimer, Bishop of Worcester, both of whom were burned at Oxford on 16 October 1555.
